judgments.why: The guide states that GitHub OAuth apps are entirely self-serve and can be created instantly without a manual review queue.
The guide explicitly states that you can enter up to 10 callback URLs.
The guide does not mention redirect_uri_mismatch errors for unmatched callback URLs.
The guide does not mention the REST API rate limit of 5,000 per hour per user.
The guide does not mention GitHub's recommendation of GitHub Apps over OAuth apps.
The guide does not mention activating Public Distribution to install the app outside your own workspace.
The guide explicitly states that the redirect_uri must use HTTPS.
The guide contains no information regarding rate limits for conversations.history based on distribution type and date.
The guide states that production takes 1-7 days, which contradicts a review taking up to 10 weeks.
The guide does not state any requirement about the app being installed on at least 10 active workspaces for Marketplace submission.
The guide does not mention the 100 test user limit for Apps in Testing status.
The guide does not mention that test-user authorizations or refresh tokens expire after seven days in Testing mode.
The guide does not state that apps accessing restricted-scope data require an annual third-party security assessment.
The guide does not specify that restricted scope verification can take several weeks (it only mentions 1-14 days generally).
The guide does not mention brand verification or that it takes 2-3 business days.
The guide lists the scopes as sensitive, but does not state whether full mailbox access or gmail.readonly are restricted scopes.
The guide states that newly created apps begin in development mode and up to 5 authenticated Spotify users can use an app in development mode.
The guide does not mention that every user must be added to the app's allowlist in development mode.
The guide does not mention whether the app owner needs Spotify Premium.
The guide does not mention restrictions on extended quota regarding organizations versus individuals or dates.
The guide does not mention any monthly active user requirement for extended quota.
The guide explicitly states that localhost is not allowed as redirect URI and that you should use HTTPS unless using a loopback address.
The guide does not mention risk-based step-up consent or user consent restrictions for newly registered multitenant apps.
The guide states that publisher verification uses a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account associated with the app registration.
The guide does not state that redirect URIs must use https or discuss localhost exceptions.
The guide does not mention whether redirect URIs are case-sensitive.
The guide does not mention tenant admins restricting user consent to apps from verified publishers.
The guide does not mention Starter tier default connections or tiers by name.
The guide does not mention the Core tier or connection limits for it.
The guide does not discuss listing on the Xero App Store or tier requirements for listing.
The guide states cost is Free, but does not mention the Core tier pricing.
The guide does not mention tier requirements for app certification.
The guide mentions free to standard paid tiers, but does not state that the X API uses pay-per-usage pricing with no subscriptions.
The guide does not mention buying credits upfront in the Developer Console.
The guide does not state that different endpoints have different costs.
The guide does not mention Business Verification or advanced access requirements.
The guide does not mention Marketing API call thresholds or Full Access requirements.
The guide does not mention the renaming of Standard Access to Limited Access or Advanced Access to Full Access.

notes: Both runs used gemini-3.5-flash-lite for every step: the free tier caps Flash models at 20 requests/day/model and that cap was hit during gold drafting. Earlier Flash runs produced richer drafts (e.g. Strava: 16 claims).

Reading: what the live agent states is reliable (precision and citation validity high) but shallow (low recall). It reads ~7 pages and misses facts on deep policy pages. That is why the library ships curated gold guides and labels live guides unreviewed.

v1→v2: llms.txt index, product-path probing and fetch-verified docs hints lifted recall and citations but not difficulty agreement; the agent underrates gated providers (Spotify, Meta) when it never reaches the gating page.
Judge = verifier model; spot-checked by hand (e.g. GitHub gh-2 stated / gh-4 absent confirmed against the raw guide). Per-fact judgments are in eval/results.json.
Ground-truth facts: 38, each with a verbatim quote re-verified live (scripts/check-ground-truth.mts). Human confirmation pending (confirmedBy).
